headline: 1,104 dead as measles outbreak kills over 1,100 in Bangladesh
summary: The DGHS reports 2.11 lakh cases since March, with hospitalizations continuing despite emergency vaccination campaigns.
details: The death toll from measles and measles-like symptoms has reached 1,104, with five more deaths reported in a single 24-hour period, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the total fatalities, 101 cases were confirmed as measles, while 1,003 were suspected cases.
Since March 15, a total of 2.11 lakh people have been diagnosed with measles or measles-like symptoms, with 1,339 new cases reported in the last 24 hours.
Hospitalizations remain high, with 1,186 patients admitted in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of hospitalised patients to 1,68,655.
Bangladesh has been facing an unprecedented outbreak since March this year, leading to the government conducting emergency vaccination campaigns in April, May, and late July.
Despite these mop-up vaccination efforts, the DGHS reports that deaths and hospital admissions continue to rise.

headline_marked: £900m breach: [[Man City found guilty of all financial charges]] by Premier League
headline: £900m breach: Man City found guilty of all financial charges by Premier League
summary: An independent commission ruled that the club used 'sham contracts' to artificially inflate revenue and reduce costs between 2009 and 2018.
details: The Premier League announced that an independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of all charges regarding serious financial breaches occurring between 2009 and 2018.
The commission found that the club used 'sham contracts' to artificially inflate revenue and reduce costs over a nine-year period.
These financial irregularities amounted to a £900 million ($1.19 billion) variation in the club's accounts.
The breaches were reportedly funded by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, the entity that owned the club during that time.
Manchester City expressed disappointment and surprise at the findings, describing them as an 'opinion' of the commission.
The club has vowed to be 'relentless' in its bid to prove its innocence and intends to pursue an appeal.
The deadline for the club to file its appeal is set for October 2.
The Premier League stated that the club systematically broke the league's rules, while sanctions will be addressed separately by the commission.
caption:
£900 million in 'sham contracts'. Manchester City has been found guilty of all financial breach charges by the Premier League.

The Premier League announced that an independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of all charges regarding serious financial breaches occurring between 2009 and 2018.

The commission found that the club used 'sham contracts' to artificially inflate revenue and reduce costs over a nine-year period.

These financial irregularities amounted to a £900 million ($1.19 billion) variation in the club's accounts.

The breaches were reportedly funded by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd, the entity that owned the club during that time.

Manchester City expressed disappointment and surprise at the findings, describing them as an 'opinion' of the commission.

The club has vowed to be 'relentless' in its bid to prove its innocence and intends to pursue an appeal.

The deadline for the club to file its appeal is set for October 2.

The Premier League stated that the club systematically broke the league's rules, while sanctions will be addressed separately by the commission.
